question.text: If $7=5+\frac{1}{7}(5+\alpha)+\frac{1}{7^2}(5+2 \alpha)+\frac{1}{7^3}(5+3 \alpha)+\ldots \infty$, then the value of $\alpha$ is :

solution.text:
$S=a+(a+d) r+(a+2 d) r^2+\ldots$
Then $S=\frac{a}{1-r}+\frac{d r}{(1-r)^2},|r| < 1$
Since, $r=\frac{1}{7}$ and $a=5, d=\alpha$
$\begin{aligned}
& 7=\frac{5}{1-\frac{1}{7}}+\frac{\alpha \cdot \frac{1}{7}}{\left(1-\frac{1}{7}\right)^2} \\
& \Rightarrow \alpha=6
\end{aligned}$
